evidence: Independently read all 10 pages using PyMuPDF of C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Sattele and Ortiz (2025) - AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams.pdf. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 411), sections 3.1 and 3.3, reports 19 students organized into eight teams. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 412), section 3.3, explicitly states that AI tools were assigned randomly to groups; Table 1 lists the different AI configurations. On the same page, section 4 states that two design experts evaluated the final outputs for overall creativity using the Consensual Assessment Technique. Results on PDF pp. 4-8 provide qualitative findings rather than numerical creativity scores or between-configuration estimates. That absence is accurately disclosed in the c898 row of C:/Users/German/Dropbox/Admin/website/ai-skill-atlas/docs/creativity-screening-2026-10-04.md, line 1656. The introduction to that report section, line 1637, explicitly says these small randomized studies are listed and omitted from the dataset whatever their outcome; it does not say every listed study otherwise qualifies for the core. C:/Dropbox/Admin/website/ai-skill-atlas/docs/creativity-codebook.md, section 3 (lines 30-44), permits randomized comparisons of different AI configurations, requires assessment of participants' outputs, and lists randomized studies below 50 participants separately from the dataset. It does not require publication of a numerical between-arm result for that screening list. Section 5 describes the arms of an ai_design contrast; it does not make availability of such an estimate a prerequisite for listing a small randomized study. The blank contrast fields in forms/c898.json therefore do not establish the auditor's proposed exclusion or a failure of criterion 3. report-data.json assigns small, consistently with tools/build_report.py lines 150-154. No correction is supported by the cited sources.
